start.name: Amreyah Cement plant (Amreyah Cement Company / former Blue Circle-Lafarge/Titan works), Kilo 55 Alexandria-Matrouh (North Coast) Road, Alexandria Governorate, Egypt
start.coord_basis: Named-facility coordinate embedded in cemnet.com's Global Cement Report facility page for 'Amreyah' (JS vars latf/lngf on the page). Independently corroborated: the company's own site states the plant sits at 'Kilo 55, Alexandria-Matrouh North Coast Road' -- a haversine check from this coordinate to Alexandria city center returns ~56.1 km, matching 'Kilo 55' almost exactly, which rejects a competing protenders.com 'head office' coordinate (~36.4 km from Alexandria, inconsistent with Kilo 55).

end.name: Borg El Arab (town center), Alexandria Governorate, Egypt
end.coord_basis: OSM Nominatim town-center node for Borg El Arab. Sheet's own EndPrefecture/District is literally 'Borg El Arab' with no more specific facility named anywhere I could find, so this is a reduced-accuracy town-level anchor per the brief's allowance (the line's stated terminus is the town's gas distribution take-off, not a named single plant). Straight-line distance to the cement-plant start is ~8.4 km, plausible for a stated 14 km pipeline with modest routing overhead.

corridor_desc: Short lateral running roughly west-southwest from the Amreyah Cement works (on the Alexandria-Matrouh North Coast Road at Kilo 55, in the industrial belt southwest of Alexandria/Amreya) to the Borg El Arab area, which hosts Egypt's Borg El Arab industrial zone and airport. Both points sit on/near the same North Coast Road corridor, so the pipeline most plausibly parallels that road rather than cutting cross-country.

facts.source: EGAS Annual Report 2018 (sheet seed ref) for length/diameter/status; I could not find a second, independently authored document naming this exact 12-inch/14 km lateral -- only the EGAS report and the sheet's own metadata cite it. The cement-plant and Borg-El-Arab endpoint identifications themselves are corroborated (see notes), but the pipeline's own existence rests on one primary source.

notes: Checked against P6032 'Borg El Arab-Midor Gas pipeline' (10 km/24in, per the GGIT snapshot) to rule out a duplicate: different diameter (24in vs this line's 12in), different named endpoint (Midor refinery vs Amreyah Cement), and a different length -- concluded these are two distinct, geographically nearby but non-duplicate laterals feeding the same industrial corridor, not the same physical line under two names. Two independent sources agree on the cement plant's coordinate (cemnet.com's embedded lat/lng + the company's own 'Kilo 55' address, cross-checked by haversine distance from Alexandria). Borg El Arab town center is a single-source (OSM) reduced-accuracy anchor since no more specific facility name for this pipeline's terminus could be found; recommend RouteAccuracy no better than 'low'. Could not locate a second source (beyond EGAS 2018) documenting this specific pipeline's existence, so facts.source is thin -- flagging for awareness rather than withholding resolution, since both endpoint place-identities are independently well-supported.

start.name: Amreya/El-Ameriya industrial-refining cluster (General Petroleum/Western Desert Gas Complex area), Amreya, Alexandria Governorate, Egypt
start.coord_basis: OSM-named node 'Amerya refinery' in the same Amreya industrial cluster (Industrial Nahda Zone) that GASCO's own company-profile PDF places its Western Desert Gas Complex (WDGC) in ('in the General Petroleum Region in Amereya'), and that other GEM-adjacent geometry in the routes repo also anchors in this same cluster (not cited as a source, used only to sanity-check plausibility). No OSM feature is tagged specifically 'WDGC', so this is a cluster-level anchor, medium confidence, rather than one exact valve pad.

end.name: Dahshour valve room on the Amriya-Dahshour 32-inch pipeline (western-desert plateau, east of the Fayum road), Giza Governorate, Egypt
end.coord_basis: Precise DMS coordinate (long 31 deg05'49" E, lat 29 deg53'24" N) given in a 2005 PETROSAFE Environmental and Social Impact Assessment for the EIB-financed Dahshour-Elkorimat pipeline, which explicitly states its own route 'starts from valve room on Amriya-Dahshour 32-inch pipeline ... eastern of Fayum road' -- i.e. this valve room is a documented point ON P8032 itself, named by an independent primary EIA document, not a guess. Cross-checked against OpenStreetMap: a bus stop named 'Masaken dahshour Terminal' (likely a GASCO-workers' housing settlement) sits at 29.8916N/31.0649E, ~3 km from this point, consistent with an industrial/compressor-station area here rather than at the Nile-valley Dahshur village further east.

corridor_desc: Runs south from the Amreya/El-Ameriya refining and gas-processing cluster on Alexandria's southeast edge, down the western edge of the Nile Delta (west of the Delta's cultivated land, roughly paralleling the desert road corridor toward the Fayum road), to a valve-room/compressor-station site in the desert plateau west of the Nile at Dahshour, Giza Governorate -- i.e. this line stays on the desert (west) side rather than crossing into the Delta or the Nile valley itself; the Dahshour-Elkorimat line then continues east from this same point, crossing the Nile near El Koraimat.

facts.source: EGAS Annual Report 2018 (sheet seed ref) for length/diameter; independently confirmed as a real, separately-named line ('Amriya-Dahshour 32-inch pipeline') by the 2005 PETROSAFE/EIB Dahshour-Elkorimat EIA, which treats it as existing infrastructure that a newer line ties into.

notes: DUPLICATE CHECK (per brief): compared against the GGIT snapshot's Western Desert Gas Pipeline complex rows (P0474/P3934, Obaiyed-Amreya Northern). Concluded NOT a duplicate: those rows run gas INTO Amreya FROM the Western Desert fields (Obaiyed/Tarek), a west-to-east/north flow; P8032 is independently documented (EIB/PETROSAFE 2005 EIA) as a separately-named 'Amriya-Dahshour 32-inch pipeline' running Amreya SOUTH to Dahshour -- i.e. gas flowing OUT of the Amreya hub toward the national grid's Upper-Egypt branch. Different direction, different independently-documented identity, geographically sequential (Western Desert feeds into Amreya, Amreya-Dahshour then distributes onward) rather than overlapping -- so treated as a distinct line, endpoints supplied rather than flagged duplicate. Flagging one open question instead: the EIB coordinate for 'Dahshour' here (29.890N/31.097E, desert plateau) is noticeably northwest of where Dahshur's Nile-valley pyramid site / village actually sits (~29.79N/31.22E); this is plausible for an industrial compressor-station siting (confirmed by a nearby OSM 'Masaken Dahshour' settlement name) but the two 'Dahshour' locations should not be conflated when this route is drawn. Amreya start-point is a cluster-level (not single-facility) anchor; recommend RouteAccuracy no better than 'low' pending a more specific WDGC/compressor-pad source.

start.name: Sadat City (El-Sadat City), Monufia Governorate, Egypt
start.coord_basis: OSM Nominatim city-center node (place=city) for Sadat City. I searched specifically for a named GASCO measurement/take-off station within Sadat City and found none in any accessible source, so this is a reduced-accuracy, city-level anchor per the brief's allowance -- the sheet's own StartLocation is 'Sadat' with no more specific facility, and the cited 2013 youm7 article and a Ministry of Petroleum project notice both describe the line simply as the 'Sadat/Dahshour' line without naming an in-city station.

end.name: Dahshour valve room on the Amriya-Dahshour/Sadat-Dahshour gas-line hub (western-desert plateau), Giza Governorate, Egypt
end.coord_basis: Same EIB/PETROSAFE-documented Dahshour valve-room point used for P8032's Dahshour end (long 31 deg05'49" E, lat 29 deg53'24" N) -- reused here because P8039 is documented as tying into the same Dahshour gas hub/compressor-station area as the Amriya-Dahshour trunk (P8032), and because this repo's own country notes record that a prior adjudication already treats the Sadat City-Dahshur 74/75 km line as a real, separate, later addition supplying Kureimat, not a duplicate of the Zaafarana-Kureimat line -- so the Dahshour-hub identity, not the specific endpoint coordinate, is what that prior adjudication settled; the coordinate itself still comes from the EIB EIA, an independent primary source.

corridor_desc: Runs south-southeast from Sadat City (Monufia Governorate, west of the Delta) down toward the Dahshour hub in the desert plateau west of the Nile in Giza Governorate, roughly paralleling the same north-south western-desert corridor that the Amreya-Dahshour trunk (P8032) also follows before that line's own valve room/tie-in point -- consistent with the youm7 article's description of the line supplying the Kureimat power plant via the Dahshour connection rather than running directly to Kureimat itself.

facts.source: youm7.com 2013 article (already cited on the sheet row) for length/diameter/year/cost and the Kureimat-supply purpose; independently corroborated by a separate Ministry of Petroleum project-approval notice (almasdar.com) that references 'the existing Sadat/Dahshour 42-inch gas line' by that exact name when approving a different, later connecting project -- confirming the line's existence and 42-inch diameter from a source with no textual dependency on youm7, though it does not repeat the 74/75 km length figure or the Kureimat-supply detail.

notes: DUPLICATE CHECK (per brief): this repo's own country notes record a prior adjudication that the Sadat City-Dahshur ~75 km line is 'a second, later Kureimat supply, not a competing identity' relative to the Zaafarana-Kureimat (P8014) line documented in a World Bank ICR -- i.e. already resolved as distinct, not a duplicate; I am not citing that internal note as an output source, only using it to confirm I'm not re-litigating a settled question. Independently searched Arabic-language sources for a second corroborating source beyond youm7 (per rule 4): found a Ministry of Petroleum project-approval notice (almasdar.com/164809) that names 'the existing Sadat/Dahshour 42-inch gas line' verbatim while approving an unrelated connecting project -- a genuinely independent government-notice source, though it only corroborates existence + diameter, not the 74 km length or exact 2013 date/cost (those remain single-sourced to youm7). Also checked a petro-news.com roundup of ~39 GASCO-era gas projects; it lists several other Dahshour-adjacent lines (Dahshour-El Wasta 65km/36in, New Capital-Dahshour 'Siemens' 70km/32in, Noubareya-Sadat 70km/36in) but none matching this exact Sadat-Dahshour identity, which is consistent with this being an older (2013) line predating that roundup's newer-project list rather than evidence against it. Sadat City start point is a city-level (not station-level) anchor since no named in-city GASCO facility could be found; Dahshour end reuses P8032's EIB-sourced valve-room coordinate on the reasoning that both lines converge on the same documented hub -- flagging this reuse candidly since it is an inference (same named hub, not a second independently-surveyed coordinate for this specific line's own tie-in point). Recommend RouteAccuracy no better than 'low'.
